# visualtone — LLM authoring guide

Music = colored curves over time. Audio is a pure function of curve data.

## Axes
- t (seconds): time / x
- y (MIDI float 0–127): pitch
- size (0–1): gain / stroke width
- hue (0–360°): timbre family (ring of synth anchors)
- lightness (0–1): brightness → spectral tilt + filter cutoff (default 0.5). Cutoff = fundamental × 1.5·32^lightness (cap 18 kHz): 0.3 ≈ 4.4×, 0.5 ≈ 8.5×, 0.7 ≈ 17×, 0.9 ≈ 34×. Stabs/leads need ~0.6+ to reach the 2–6 kHz presence band.
- saturation (0–1, optional): 1 = pure tone, lower = more noise ("grey = noisy")

## Curve syntax (points)
Optional per point:
- ease: step | linear | in | out | inOut | exp — how to **arrive** at this point
- tween: seconds — only the last `tween` seconds before this point interpolate

Defaults when ease omitted:
- size 0 → >0: step (instant attack)
- size falling: exp
- both size 0: silence between
- pitch while sounding: linear (legato); use silence between notes for staccato

## Notes shorthand
```json
{ "t": 0, "y": 36, "size": 0.9, "duration": 0.15, "ease": "exp" }
```
- hold (default): sustain then ~20ms release
- exp: exponential decay over duration (drums, hats)

## Hue families
0° kick, 30° bass, 70° pluck, 110° bell/keys, 160° supersaw lead, 210° pad, 260° vocal, 300° snare/clap, 335° hi-hat

## Track FX (optional)
- `channel`: `0` or `[0,1]` stereo route from one mono curve
- `space`: hall reverb send 0–1 (visual: glow). Shared stereo FDN, not a per-track reverb.
- `room`: short room send 0–1, a second shared bus (`master.room`)
- `echo`: delay send 0–1
- `release`: tail after the note curve, milliseconds. 0 (default) is a hard cut.
- `chorus`: `{ "depth": 0.4, "rateHz": 0.4, "mix": 0.35 }` — 3 modulated delays after the track comp
- `duck`: `{ "by": "kick-drum", "amount": 0.6 }`
- `timbre`: partial override of internal synth vector
  - `velocity` 0–1: louder notes open the filter (`cutoff *= 2^(velocity*(size-0.7)*2)`), quieter notes darken it. 0 = off.
  - `drift` 0–1: slow per-voice pitch drift (±6 cents × drift), per-onset cutoff jitter, random unison phase. Seeded, so renders stay reproducible. 0 does not touch the noise sequence.
- `bpm` + `master`: `{ "loudness": -14, "saturation": 0.3, "reverb": { "size": 0.7, "decay": 0.6, "preDelayMs": 25, "damping": 0.4, "width": 0.85 }, "room": { "size": 0.4, "decay": 0.3, "preDelayMs": 8 }, "delay": { "beats": 0.75 }, "eq": { "highShelf": { "freq": 8000, "gain": 2 } }, "comp": { "threshold": -9, "ratio": 2 }, "limiter": { "ceiling": -1, "releaseMs": 60 } }`
  - Master chain: sum → `eq` → `saturation` (even harmonics + DC block, skipped at 0) → `comp` → drive → loudness match → lookahead limiter (always on, 5 ms lookahead, ceiling -1 dBFS, also watches 4× intersample peaks). Raising `loudness` makes the limiter work harder and lowers the peak-to-loudness ratio.
  - `reverb.damping` is how fast highs die in the tail. `preDelayMs` defaults to 25 on the hall and 8 on the room.
- Mono tracks on `channel: 0` play in the LEFT speaker only when the score is stereo; put kick/bass on `[0,1]` to center them.

## Mixing / modulation / groove (optional)
- `eq`: `{ lowCut, highCut, lowShelf: {freq, gain}, highShelf: {freq, gain}, peaks: [{freq, gain, q}] }` (Hz, dB)
- `comp`: `{ threshold: -18, ratio: 3, attackMs: 10, releaseMs: 120, knee: 6, makeup: 0 }`
- `lfo`: `[{ target: lightness|pitch|gain|pan, depth, rate (Hz) | beats (period), shape: sine|triangle|saw|square, phase }]`
  - lightness depth = ±brightness offset; pitch depth = ±semitones; gain depth = dip 0–1; pan +1 = right
- `automation`: `{ lightness: [{t, v}], gain: [{t, v}] }` — linear; lightness v is an offset, gain v a multiplier
- score `swing` 0–1 (1 = triplet), `swingGrid` 8|16; track `swing` overrides
- `humanize`: `{ timeMs, size }` deterministic jitter per note
- Mix tips: pads quiet (size ~0.1–0.15 when sustained), lowCut everything except kick/bass, duck pads/stabs by kick.

## Output
CLI `--bit-depth 16|24|32f` (16 default with TPDF dither), `--no-dither`.

## Example: deep house v7 (same arrangement, wetter and less mechanical)
See examples/deep-house-v7.json (generated by examples/scripts/deep-house-v7.mjs). Adds a pure sub plus a saturated mid bass, a keys layer, `release` on stabs and keys, hall and room sends, `timbre.velocity` / `timbre.drift`, chorus, and `master.saturation`. Tuned until `analyze --profile deep-house` reported no findings. Replacing the old per-track reverb changes any older score that uses `space`; previously rendered WAVs are unchanged.

## Clips (external audio)

TTS stays outside visualtone. Render WAV, then:

```json
{ "id": "voice", "role": "voice", "clip": { "src": "tts/scene2.wav", "at": 3.2, "gain": 1, "fadeIn": 0.05, "fadeOut": 0.08, "trim": [0, 4.1] } }
```

`clips` is the same shape as an array. The library does not read files: pass decoded audio as `render(score, { clips: { "tts/scene2.wav": { sampleRate, buffers, sha256 } } })`. The CLI loads paths relative to the score and records sha256 on `result.inputs` and on the analysis report.

Duck a bed under speech: `{ "by": "voice", "amount": 0.5, "holdMs": 80, "releaseMs": 280, "band": [1000, 4000] }`. `band` ducks only that range with `out = x − (1−g)·bandpass(x)` (0 dB-peak RBJ bandpass, f0 = √(f1·f2), Q = f0/(f2−f1)); the center gain equals the duck gain. `holdMs` stops the music pumping between words.

## Sound effects

A track `sfx` array expands into curve tracks (`role: "sfx"`, ids like `fx:whoosh-0`) before render.

| name | use | params |
|------|-----|--------|
| whoosh | transition | `direction` -1..1 (pan travel), `brightness`, `duration`, `pan`, `size` |
| riser | build into a cut | `duration`, `brightness`, `size` |
| swell | soft entrance | `duration`, `brightness`, `size`, `pitch` or `y` |
| impact | hit | `low` 0..1 (boom amount), `tail` seconds, `size`, `brightness` |
| pop | UI click | `pitch`/`y`, `brightness`, `size` |
| tick | small mark | `brightness`, `size` |
| key | single bell note | `pitch`/`y`, `duration`, `size` |
| shimmer | sparkle tail | `duration`, `brightness`, `size`, `pitch`/`y` |

```json
{ "id": "fx", "sfx": [{ "sfx": "whoosh", "t": 4.0, "duration": 0.4, "size": 0.7, "direction": 0.6 }] }
```

## Segments

`mix([{ score, at, fadeIn, fadeOut, prefix }], master)` places each score on the outer timeline. Groove runs in segment-local time before the shift. A segment `master` is ignored (warning); the argument wins. JSON form, loaded by the CLI: `{ "segments": [{ "src": "scene2.json", "at": 4.0, "fadeIn": 0.2, "prefix": "s2/" }] }`.

Track `offset` shifts one track. Track `seed` keeps noise stable when tracks are reordered.

## Picture data

`render(score, { envelopes: { fps: 30 } })` returns `envelopes.tracks[id].onsets` (seconds) and `.level` (RMS per frame, after the strip and duck, before sends). Frame i covers `[i/fps, (i+1)/fps)`. `envelopes.master.level` is after the limiter. CLI: `--envelopes env.json --fps 30`.

## Musical spelling

With `bpm` (and optional `meter`, default `[4, 4]`): point/note `at: "4:2"` (bar 4, beat 2, 1-based), `pitch: "A3"`, note `len: "1/8"`. Missing bpm is an error. `chord("Am7", "A3")` and `pattern("x...x..x", { bpm, y, bar, step })` are functions, not schema.

## Acoustic engines

`engine`: `wavetable` (default) | `pluck` (Karplus–Strong) | `marimba` (modal) | `epiano` (FM). The three acoustic engines are polyphonic: overlapping notes are not cut. Hue does not interpolate with the wavetable ring; it changes brightness or inharmonicity.

## Voiceover profile

`analyze --profile voiceover-bed`. Set track `role` to `voice`, `sfx`, or `music`. Checks: music yields 1–4 kHz while the voice is active, sfx does not mask the music, sfx is not too dense. Band shares and warmth count only `role: "music"` tracks, and suggestions name those track ids. `master.lufs` is a BS.1770 target and replaces the RMS `master.loudness` match when set; `render().master.loudnessDb` and the CLI line then report the measured LUFS. Default `sampleRate` is 48000; existing examples that write 44100 stay 44100.

## Static pan

Track `pan` is -1..1 (0 = center, equal-power). `automation.pan` is an offset added to it, so a whoosh can travel. `automation.lightness` stays an offset and `automation.gain` stays a multiplier.

## Listening loop
The way to hear a render without ears: render, analyze, read the PNG, edit the score from findings, diff.

1. `npx visualtone analyze score.json --profile deep-house --json report.json --png report.png`
   - `.json` renders with stems (masking + per-track share). `.wav` is mix-only (16/24 PCM, 32-bit float).
   - `--panel spectrogram|curves|stems|bands|loudness|phase|kick|masking|ssm|space|dynamics` writes one panel.
   - Texture metrics (json scores only): `warmth` is the 150–500 Hz share. `space.wetShare` is hall+room+delay bus energy over dry stems plus those buses (needs a score render, not a wav). `space.tailRatioDb` is the median tail-vs-attack level. `dynamics.hitVariationDb` is the 25th percentile of per-track local hit-level deviation (tracks with at least 16 hits; a section fade is not counted). `dynamics.repetition` is the fraction of bar pairs 4 or 8 bars apart with similarity above 0.98. `stereo.bandSideMidDb` splits side/mid into low, mid, and high.
2. Read `report.json` findings first. Each has `severity`, `message`, `suggestion` naming a score field (`channel`, `size`, `eq.peaks`, `automation.gain`, `master.comp`, `room`, `release`, `timbre.velocity`, `timbre.drift`, `humanize.size`).
3. Built-in profiles: `deep-house`, `techno`, `pop-edm`, `ambient`, `voiceover-bed`. Numbers are mixing experience, not a standard. `npx visualtone profile ref.wav -o my.json` builds one from references (do not commit the wav).
4. `npx visualtone diff before.json after.json` lists metric deltas and which findings appeared or went away.
5. Optional taste log, one JSON object per line in `feedback/ratings.jsonl`:
   `{"date":"2026-10-06","file":"examples/deep-house-v5.json","reportHash":"…","scores":{"groove":4,"timbre":3,"clarity":4,"overall":3},"note":""}`
   Scores are 1–5. Do not invent a rating the user did not give.

What the pictures show: score curves (pitch vs time), log spectrogram, one row per stem, band shares, short-term LUFS, phase scatter, kick envelope, masking matrix, self-similarity + chroma, space (bus wet bars and the tail curve), dynamics (one dot per hit; a straight row is a mechanical part).

## Timbre measurement

For tuning one instrument, not a mix.

- `npx visualtone timbre note.wav --midi 60 [--ref ref.wav] [--json out.json]` measures one note: f0 and cents, pitch stability, glide, vibrato; attack 10–90%, decay dB/s (overall, early, late), T60, release after `--note-off`; partials 1–16 in dB, slope dB/oct, odd/even, inharmonicity B (f_n = n·f0·√(1+B·n²)), HNR, spurious peaks off the partial series (aliasing), per-partial decay for 1–8; centroid, flatness, log-mel, MFCC; clicks, DC, NaN. A score input renders first; `--track id` picks a stem.
- With `--ref`, `compareTimbre` scores each metric against a tolerance (error ≤ 1 passes) and turns the misses into findings, worst first. The reference must be a single note at the same pitch, 44.1 kHz or more.
- `npx visualtone probe track.json [--pitches 36,48,60,72,84] [--sizes 0.3,0.6,0.9] [--note 1.5] [--tail 2] [--ref dir] [--wav probe.wav]` plays one track template over a pitch × size grid and measures the dry stem. Findings check habits most acoustic instruments share: in tune, louder and brighter with size, higher notes decay sooner, no clicks. Reference files are named `60.wav` or `60_0.9.wav`.
- Library: `analyzeNote(buffer, sampleRate, { start, stop, noteOff, midi })`, `compareTimbre(ours, ref)`, `probeTrack(track, opts)`, `analyzeProbe(mono, sampleRate, cells)`.

CLI: `npx visualtone render score.json -o out.wav`
Schema: `npx visualtone schema`
